records.name: Slow Food Philadelphia
records.summary: Philadelphia's local chapter of Slow Food, a movement for better food. It hosts dinners, talks and social events, gives an award to local food businesses, and lists farms, farm stands and community supported agriculture shares.
records.what_you_do: Come to a member dinner or a public event such as the October banquet, join as a member, or sign up for volunteer work through the group's volunteer page.

schedule.text: Member and public events are posted on the site. The next listed event is a banquet on Thursday, October 22, 2026 at 6:00 pm in Queen Village.

locations.label: Queen Village, the October banquet on 3rd Street

cost.text: Banquet tickets are $30. Member dues are not listed on the page.

first_step.how: Buy a $30 ticket for the October 22, 2026 banquet, or join as a member through the site's join page.
first_step.basis: Events and membership are posted publicly with a clear way to sign up, though the page does not say what membership costs.

records.notes: The IRS legal name is Slow Food USA Inc. The 736 Manton St address and EIN come from the lead file. The site belongs to the Philadelphia chapter and does not show the EIN, so the match to the legal entity is not confirmed on the page. The home page lists an October 22, 2026 banquet and also says no events are scheduled; the banquet listing is the evidence used. Crowd is inferred from a BYOB dinner listing, not stated. The contact page is at slowfoodphilly.org/contact-us/; no email or phone is published on the home page.

records.name: Spruce Foundation
records.summary: An all-volunteer Philadelphia group that raises money and gives grants to youth-serving nonprofits. Members join a donor council or the board to help choose grants and run events.
records.what_you_do: Spruce Council members make a donation, attend at least two Spruce events, and work on one project each board year, which runs August to July. Board members serve on committees such as grants and events.

schedule.text: Board applications open once a year in the spring. Spruce Council interest is accepted year round. The events calendar is linked, but no dated events are listed on the page.

cost.text: Council membership asks for a meaningful donation. The amount is not listed.

first_step.how: Fill out the Spruce Council interest form on the Get Involved page, which is open year round, or watch for the spring board application.
first_step.basis: Council membership needs a donation, two events and a project in the board year, so the way in is a commitment before you see the group.

records.notes: The legal name is Spruce Foundation Inc, and PO Box 2377 comes from the lead file. The site calls it an all-volunteer 501(c)(3) that gives grants to youth-serving nonprofits. The 2026 grants are dated to the year only, so no month is recorded and the active status rests on that year. The page does not say whether it is a private foundation or a public charity, and private foundations are out of scope. Please confirm its public charity status before it goes live. The 2026 grantees named on the site (Black Girls Love Math, Ginger Arts Center, Hunting Park United, MLPML) were not checked and are not added as leads, because no URLs were captured. Its Facebook, Instagram and LinkedIn pages exist but their links were not captured.

records.name: Stories In My Backyard
records.summary: A Philadelphia media arts group that teaches photography, film and virtual reality to Black youth, with Black instructors. It also stages public photo exhibits about Philadelphia's Black music history.
records.what_you_do: Students in the Exposure photography program learn to shoot and print pictures. The group also takes volunteers and team members for its exhibit and fundraising work, and visitors can see its outdoor and pop-up exhibits.

schedule.text: Youth programs run through partner schools and libraries, and exhibits and fundraisers pop up through the year. Dates are posted on Instagram, Linktree and Eventbrite.

locations.label: Philadelphia, programs at partner schools, libraries and pop-up exhibits

cost.text: Program cost is not stated. Donations are welcome, and some events are free or ask for a suggested $5 donation.

first_step.how: Follow the group on Instagram or use Linktree to find the next exhibit or workshop, or use the take action page on storiesinmybackyard.org to volunteer or join the team.
first_step.basis: Public exhibits and a volunteer route are posted openly, though youth program seats are for enrolled students.

records.notes: The legal name is Stories in My Backyard Inc. The April 25, 2026 Penn Relays media team item is from the group's own website. Youth programs are for Black students, while exhibits and volunteering are open to the public, so open_to is public and community is black. Partners named on the site (the Free Library, PSTV, The Academy at Penn) are institutions and were not added as leads. The site has no general email or phone number.

records.name: PA4WN Lab
records.notes: The lab operates as a DBA of T. Alexander Foundation Inc, a 501(c)(3). Its page describes workshops, keynotes, consulting and merchandise for athletes, schools, social service groups and companies, but does not say how the public can attend, join or volunteer. The Get Involved page returned a 404. The old pa4wn.org and pa4wn.com addresses redirect to the lab's site. Hidden as a private foundation with no public way in. A reviewer should re-check if its workshops are open to the public.

records.name: The Evoluer House
records.summary: A Philadelphia nonprofit for teen girls, especially girls of color in urban areas. It runs eight week programs in personal development, job readiness and podcasting, and keeps an alumnae network.
records.what_you_do: Girls enroll in one of the eight week programs to build confidence, job skills and, for alumnae, podcast skills. Families sign up for the email list to hear when registration opens, since there is a waiting list.

schedule.text: Programs run as eight week sessions when registration opens. The programs page says Summer 2027 sign ups are taken by email alert. No specific start dates are listed.

cost.text: No tuition or fees are listed. The site asks for donations.

first_step.how: Join the email list at evoluerhouse.org/emailupdates so you hear when Summer 2027 registration opens, then reply right away because there is a waiting list.
first_step.basis: Registration runs through a waiting list, and the page does not explain the application steps or eligibility for every program.

records.notes: The newest dated item found is a November 19, 2021 news report referenced on the site. The programs page and footer mention 2026 and Summer 2027, but those references are undated, so the status follows the newest dated evidence. A reviewer should confirm with the group that these programs still run before this goes live. The page's impact claims were not used. The legal name is The Evoluer House, and the programs are described as taking place virtually, a notice that is also undated.

records.name: The Krimson Foundation
records.notes: Both https://www.krimsonfoundation.org and https://krimsonfoundation.org returned only the words 'Contact Support', with no description of the organization, its programs or any way to take part. Hidden under the IRS foundation rule after the fetch allowed for these records. The name suggests a foundation. A reviewer with a browser may re-check.

records.name: The Rescue Express
records.summary: A foster based dog rescue that takes dogs from high kill shelters, mainly in the South, and places them with foster homes and adopters. It has no kennel.
records.notes: The IRS filing address is 1030 Annin St, 19147, in South Philadelphia. The group's site gives Media, PA as its base and describes dog rescue mainly in the South. No Philadelphia program, event or volunteer shift was found. Marked out of area. A reviewer may change this if a Philadelphia drop off or foster site exists. The adoption and foster pages linked from the site were not read, and the join form link was not submitted.

records.name: TheatreXP Philadelphia
records.notes: Could not read the group's site. https://theatrexp.org, https://www.theatrexp.org and its /about page all return an expired certificate. The Theatre Philadelphia directory listing for the group returned 403 when read. One search snippet (not a page read) described a Philadelphia nonprofit theatre company formed in 2010 to develop original plays, and gave theatrexp.org as its site. No dated activity was confirmed, so status is unknown. What a visitor can do (attend, take a class, volunteer) is not established. Retry later with the site or the directory page.

records.name: United We Heal Film Festival
records.notes: The website https://www.unitedweheal.com failed to load on two tries (socket closed), and on a later try it redirected to a domain sale page, so the group's own site appears to be gone. Both searches were used up on groups with unusable sites, so no other source was found. Nothing about events, dates or how to take part is established. A later agent should search for the festival by name. This record is intentionally incomplete and will be held back until someone can confirm it.

records.name: UrbEd Advocates
records.summary: A youth led Philadelphia group that does organizing and policy work to win more money and better conditions for public schools.
records.what_you_do: Students and young adults can join as organizers, interns or fellows, testify at school board meetings, sign petitions, or use the Youth Space in Center City. Most open roles are for Philadelphia high school and college students.

schedule.text: Organizing roles and a year long paid fellowship are posted on the careers and fellowship pages, with no dates shown. The Youth Space can be reserved or visited.

cost.text: Joining, testifying and signing petitions are free. The fellowship pays participants.

first_step.how: Use the Meet with us button on urbedadvocates.org to contact the group, or check the Careers page for open organizing roles.
first_step.basis: The site names several open routes (contact, careers, fellowship, testimony sign ups) and does not show an application step for the basic ways in.

records.notes: The IRS legal name is Urbed. The group calls itself UrbEd Advocates and the site mentions UrbEd Inc. The homepage statements carry no dates, and no dated events were listed, so probably_active rests on a working site alone. Public school advocacy has no exact tag, so youth_leadership is used under advocacy-rights. The asks on the site are school board testimony, a student seat petition and funding. No candidate or party work was seen.

records.name: US Chess School
records.summary: A nonprofit that gives free chess training to talented young players through camps. Camps run online year round and in person in some cities, with coaches who are grandmasters and international masters.
records.what_you_do: Players apply for an online or in person camp and are invited based on rating, experience and fit. Online camps run on weekends. The next one is an online fall camp on October 24 and 25, 2026, and its applications are not yet open.

schedule.text: Online camps run on weekends through the year. Upcoming: Fall 2026 on October 24 and 25, Winter 2027 on February 6 and 7 (girls only), and Spring 2027 on May 22 and 23. In person camps are held in major cities, and none are scheduled.

cost.text: The site says the training is provided free of charge.

first_step.how: Watch the online camp page for the Fall 2026 application window, which the site lists as not yet open, then send an application with your chess experience, rating and interests.
first_step.basis: Camps are free, but a rating based application decides who is invited, so the way in is clear but selective.

records.notes: Ages and the camp entry rules are not stated on the site. Winter 2027 is for girls only. The IRS filing address is 1336 Cypress St, 19107, but the site names no Philadelphia program, so this is listed as a national online program that Philadelphia players can join. A reviewer may decide it is out of area. The page itself was posted September 2, 2026. Its mailing list and donate pages exist, and no email or phone is published.

records.name: US-Ghana Chamber of Commerce
records.summary: A membership trade group that links businesses in the United States and Ghana. It runs trade missions, business summits and open community gatherings, and a youth volunteer program for high school students.
records.what_you_do: Business members get trade, investment and networking help, and can join trade missions and expos. Anyone can register for the public gatherings, and tri-state high school students can volunteer at large Philadelphia events through the Youth Diplomats program.

schedule.text: Trade missions, summits and community gatherings are announced on the events page. The most recent dated item is a trade mission to Accra, Ghana, May 30 to June 5, 2026, aimed at Philadelphia and Pennsylvania business leaders.

cost.text: Membership dues are not listed on the site, and event prices were not shown on the pages read.

first_step.how: Look at the membership categories page on usghcc.org to see how to join, or register for a public gathering on the events page.
first_step.basis: Membership is for businesses and the dues are not listed, so the way in is unclear for individuals; public events are open with registration.

records.notes: The batch website was typed as 'https//usghanachamberofcommerce.org', which is malformed. The corrected domain redirects to usghcc.org, which is the chamber's own site, and that is the source used. The EIN and the 909 S Fairhill St address come from the IRS lead file, not the site. The June gathering listing on the site gives no year, so it is not used for dates. The trade mission listing is on World Trade Center Central PA's events page and names the chamber as organizer. Search snippets mentioned summit dates in 2024 and 2025 that conflict with each other, so they are not used.

records.name: Vimutti Foundation
records.notes: The website given (psandco.com) is the site of P.S. & Co., a bakery, cafe and market at 1706 Locust Street, not the foundation's own site. The bakery's site has a 'Meet Our Foundation' link that points to the Vimutti Foundation, but that page's text was not captured. No public program, event or volunteer route for the foundation was found, so it is hidden under the private foundation rule. Re-check if the foundation has its own site.

records.name: Washington Square West Trust
records.notes: The trust describes itself as a grant-making foundation. It funds nonprofits whose goals match its own, and it reimburses residents for neighborhood improvements under standing grants. It holds no meetings or events, and no membership or volunteer route was found. Hidden under the private foundation rule. A reviewer may decide the resident grants make it a useful funder to list. Its Facebook page is facebook.com/WashingtonSquareWestTrust, which was not read.

records.name: The Questers
records.summary: A nonprofit membership group that began in 1944 as a group for studying antiques and now works on history, historic places and preservation. Local chapters meet to study history, raise money for preservation and share local stories.
records.what_you_do: Join a local chapter, attend its meetings, and take part in study, storytelling or restoration projects. The international headquarters on South Quince Street takes visits by appointment.

schedule.text: Chapters meet regularly, but the site gives no meeting times. Regional meetings happen once or twice a year. Headquarters visits are by appointment.

cost.text: The site does not list dues or fees.

first_step.how: Email questers210@questers1944.org or call 215-923-5183 to ask which chapter meets near you, and sign up through the Join The Questers page.
first_step.basis: Sign up is online, but the site does not say how to attend a chapter meeting as a guest or what membership costs.

records.notes: The IRS legal name is Washington State Questers. Its address matches the international headquarters at 210 S Quince St, so the record covers The Questers as a whole. The site lists no Philadelphia chapter by name and no dated events. The Washington State chapter implied by the lead is not mentioned on the site. Ask the group before listing any chapter meeting place. The headquarters contact is an administrator, not a chapter officer. Contact name in the lead: Questers Inc.

blocked.note: certificate expired on the apex, www and /about pages, so the site could not be read
directory listing for TheatreXP refused the fetch
socket closed on two tries, then redirects to a domain sale page; the group's own site appears gone

notes: All 15 batch groups were attempted. Searches: 2 of 2 used, both on groups with unusable websites (US-Ghana Chamber of Commerce, TheatreXP). Fetches: about 30 of 60 used. Verdicts: 10 publish (2 of them minimal, TheatreXP and United We Heal, which have no summary or sources and will be held back), 4 hide (3 private foundations or trusts and 1 PA4WN Lab, a foundation with no public way in), 1 out_of_area (The Rescue Express). Search budget ran out before United We Heal could be searched by name. Dropped rather than listed as leads: the four 2026 grantees named on sprucefoundation.org (no URLs captured, none guessed). The Krimson Foundation page returned only a stub. The Evoluer House is dormant on dated evidence only, although its programs page is current-looking, so it needs a human check. No record was made from a page I could not read, and no URL was guessed except the corrected chamber domain, which redirected to the chamber's own site.
